primary_modality_specific: Subcutaneous cyclic hexapeptide C5aR1 complement receptor antagonist (PMX 205)
key_quantitative_anchor: [MEASURED] Top unadopted Bye 2025 hit (#9/107: +1.3055d, p=0.0141, Wilcoxon p=0.0110, q_BH=0.0695) with zero completed C5aR1 ALS efficacy RCTs, BUT upstream human ALS C5 cleavage inhibitors failed Phase 2/3 trials (ravulizumab CHAMPION-ALS NCT04248465 N=382 & zilucoplan HEALEY NCT04436497), glia-free cortical Exc C5AR1 is minimal (2.06 log2CPM), and Bye 2025 glia-free monocultures lack exogenous or microglial complement C5/C5a ligand, making ligand-independent 2.5 uM cyclic-hexapeptide off-target activity the primary null hypothesis pending C5AR1-KO + avacopan target deconvolution.
discriminating_next_test: Execute in vitro target-deconvolution testing of PMX 205 vs orthosteric avacopan in wild-type vs C5AR1-KO human iPSC-MNs (+/- exogenous C5a & microglia, testing the primary null that 2.5 uM rescue in C5/C5a-free monocultures is a ligand-independent cyclic-hexapeptide off-target artifact rather than on-target C5aR1 blockade sparing C5b-9/C5L2), plus unbound human CSF Kp,uu quantification.

primary_modality_specific: High-dose CNS-penetrant N-acetylcysteine regimen (>=50-70 mg/kg/d parenteral or high-dose oral; distinct from low-dose <=600 mg/d oral NAC)
key_quantitative_anchor: [MEASURED] Bye 2025 Rank #12/107 (+0.9458d, p=0.0201, q_BH=0.0936, n=15) did not survive BH-FDR and may reflect extracellular thiol media buffering, YET neither clinical futility nor insurmountable CNS PK deficit is established: Louwerse et al. 1995 PMID:7763202 (50 mg/kg/d SC NAC [~3,500 mg/d at 70 kg], N=110) was an underpowered trial whose survival CI includes substantial benefit (overall HR=0.74 [95% CI 0.41-1.33], p=0.31; limb-onset n=81 HR=0.50 [0.24-1.04], p=0.06), and Katz et al. 2015 PMID:25765302 demonstrated that 70 mg/kg oral NAC BID achieves 9.26 +/- 1.62 uM human CSF NAC (p<0.001) without DLT, whereas recruiting NCT07414212 (N=90) administers 600 mg/d oral effervescent NAC (5.83x lower nominal daily mass than 3,500 mg/d SC across non-equivalent ~6-10% oral bioavailability) co-formulated with 1,800 mg/d EH301 (1,500 mg nicotinamide riboside + 300 mg pterostilbene) + 100 mg riluzole, precluding single-agent NAC attribution.
discriminating_next_test: Separate extracellular thiol media-oxidation buffering (using Catalase/GSH-ethyl-ester/GCLC-inhibition controls) from intracellular neuronal glutathione rescue in human sALS iPSC-MNs, and require paired human ALS CSF free-NAC and 7T/3T MRS cortical/cervical GSH target-engagement proof at high-dose (>=50-70 mg/kg) dosing before efficacy testing.

primary_modality_specific: High-dose oral L-serine amino-acid supplementation (15 g BID = 30 g/d) gated on mandatory SPTLC1/SPTLC2 genetic exclusion
key_quantitative_anchor: [MEASURED] Bye 2025 2.5 uM survival delta (+0.7117d, Rank #20/107, nominal p=0.04190, q_BH=0.17067 across 16 sALS lines) reflects a fixed-library-concentration endpoint mismatch where adding 2.5 uM increases ~400 uM basal BrainPhys/DMEM-F12 media L-serine concentration by only +0.625% (never testing clinical 15 g BID = 30 g/d systemic exposure); zero randomized placebo-controlled sALS efficacy trials have completed (Phase 1 NCT01835782 N=20 Levine 2017 PMID:27589995 was uncontrolled safety-only; single-arm Phase 2 NCT03580616 N=43 terminated for IRB noncompliance), while human ALS genetics establishes a mandatory <0.5% monogenic exclusion gate: SPTLC1/SPTLC2 GoF variants disrupt ORMDL ceramide feedback and overproduce canonical C18-C22 dihydrosphingolipids/ceramides where exogenous L-serine is contraindicated (Mohassel et al. 2021 PMID:34059824; Ziak et al. 2026 PMID:43025655, 10.1016/j.jlr.2026.101187; targeted by intrathecal SPTLC1 ASO LTX-002 NCT07660614).
discriminating_next_test: Quantify 1-deoxysphingolipid vs canonical C18-C22 ceramide flux and dose-response survival across physiological CSF-like low-serine (~25-40 uM) human sALS iPSC-MN media (0-1,000 uM L-serine), and enforce mandatory upfront SPTLC1/SPTLC2 sequencing + plasma sphingolipid screening before any controlled sporadic ALS trial.

gene_or_drug: CHIT1 / GPNMB / CHI3L1-CHI3L2 microglial chitinase-lysosomal staging axis
key_quantitative_anchor: [MEASURED] All four sub-nodes (C017-N1..N4) replicate strongly as symptomatic cross-sectional symptomatic-vs-asymptomatic staging and glial/lysosomal fluid biomarkers (completely flat in pre-symptomatic C9/SOD1 carriers), but fail Track B drug-target criteria: human genetic CHIT1 deficiency (rs3831317) does not alter ALS risk/progression, GPNMB is compensatory/neuroprotective (wrong sign for inhibition), and CHI3L1/CHI3L2 are catalytically inactive pseudochitinases.
discriminating_next_test: Deploy rs3831317-genotype-adjusted CSF CHIT1 + GPNMB + CHI3L1/CHI3L2 as a quantitative cross-sectional symptomatic-vs-asymptomatic staging and ALS-Glia / lysosomal pharmacodynamic biomarker panel in Track A/B trials rather than pursuing chitinase/GPNMB inhibition.

key_quantitative_anchor: [MEASURED] Bye 2025 Rank #19/107 (+0.7430d, p=0.0495, q_BH=0.1827) failed BH-FDR, and in the multicenter randomized double-blind placebo-controlled Phase II QALS trial at 2,700 mg/d over 9 months (NCT00243932, Kaufmann et al. 2009 Ann Neurol PMID:19743457, PMC2854625, N=185 [n=75 at 2,700 mg/d vs n=75 placebo]), Stage 2 primary bias-adjusted one-sided futility testing (H0: >=20% less 9-mo ALSFRS-R decline, alpha=0.10) gave p=0.14 (mean decline 8.80 vs 9.44; 0.51 was an LTF sensitivity CI bound where p=0.20), prespecified death-score (16) sensitivity met futility (p=0.025 < 0.10), post-hoc linear slope gave p=0.097, secondary endpoints (FVC, QoL, fatigue) were null, plasma CoQ10 saturated between 1,800 and 2,700 mg/d (Table 1; Ferrante et al. 2005 PMID:16344537) blocking higher oral exposure, and QALS investigators concluded Phase III was unjustified.
